speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; to begin our assessment, could you please describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallory-Weiss Tear. The history of forceful retching followed by chest pain and choking is classic for a mucosal tear at the gastroesophageal junction. I will request an Upper Endoscopy (EGD) to confirm the diagnosis and assess for active bleeding.
